Drawing pedigrees

Source: vignettes/drawing.Rmd
drawing.Rmd

pedkindraw draws a pedigree in two steps. makePedigreeMatingLayout() works out where each animal and each mating goes, and drawPedigreeDiagram() draws that layout as an interactive picture: in the RStudio viewer, in a web page or in a document such as this one. This vignette shows what a drawing shows and how to change it, one feature at a time, on small pedigrees typed in the code. The last drawing is the 375-animal example pedigree that comes with the package. In each drawing you can zoom with the mouse wheel or a trackpad, drag to move the picture, hover over an animal, and pick one in the “Select by id” box.

From a data frame to a drawing

A pedigree is a data frame with one row per animal: its id, sire, dam and sex, and the generation number gen that findGeneration() gives (vignette("pedkindraw") describes the columns). Here A and B are the parents of C, D and E, and C and F are the parents of G and H.

library(pedkindraw)

fam <- data.frame(
  id   = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F", "G", "H"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", "A", NA, "C", "C"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", "B", NA, "F", "F"),
  sex  = c("M", "F", "M", "F", "F", "F", "F", "M")
)
fam$gen <- findGeneration(fam$id, fam$sire, fam$dam)
layout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam)
drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)

Each generation is a row: A and B at the top, their offspring C, D and E below them, and G and H at the bottom. F has no parents in the pedigree, so she is a founder like A and B, but she is drawn beside her mate C, on his row. A mating is the small dot between two mates, with lines down to each of their offspring, drawn at right angles as kinship2 draws them. In each mating here the sire is drawn left of the dam, and C, D and E are drawn left to right in the order of their rows.

The layout is a list. Its nodes data frame has a row for each animal and each mating dot, and for each of the invisible points that the lines turn at, with the node’s place: x, and y, which grows downward. The ids of the dots and points start with two underscores. Its edges data frame has a row for each line.

names(layout)
#> [1] "nodes"              "edges"              "duplicateToReal"   
#> [4] "isolatedIds"        "conditions"         "conditionsNotDrawn"
#> [7] "hints"
animals <- layout$nodes[!startsWith(layout$nodes$id, "__"), ]
data.frame(id = animals$id, shape = animals$shape,
           x = round(animals$x), y = animals$y)
#>   id  shape    x   y
#> 1  A square  -10   0
#> 2  B    dot  110   0
#> 3  C square -150 150
#> 4  D    dot   90 150
#> 5  E    dot  210 150
#> 6  F    dot  -30 150
#> 7  G    dot -150 300
#> 8  H square  -30 300

Symbols and the legend

The symbol shows the sex: a square for "M", a circle for "F", a star for "H" (a hermaphrodite), a triangle for "U" (unknown) and a diamond for any other code or none (NA), “Other / Unrecorded” in the legend. An optional status column marks with a slash each animal whose status is "DECEASED". Here S1 and D1 have one offspring of each sex code, and S1 has died.

kids <- data.frame(
  id     = c("S1", "D1", "female", "male", "hermaphrodite", "unknown",
             "unrecorded"),
  sire   = c(NA, NA, "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1"),
  dam    = c(NA, NA, "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1"),
  sex    = c("M", "F", "F", "M", "H", "U", NA),
  status = c("DECEASED", "ALIVE", "ALIVE", "ALIVE", "ALIVE", "ALIVE",
             "ALIVE")
)
kids$gen <- findGeneration(kids$id, kids$sire, kids$dam)
kidsLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(kids)
drawPedigreeDiagram(kidsLayout)

The legend on the right of every drawing lists the five symbols, then “Affected” (see Conditions, below) and “Deceased”, then the lines: the dashed line that joins two places of the same animal, and the three twin lines. Hover over an animal to see its id, sex, generation, sire and dam, and each condition; hover over a mating dot to see how many offspring it has. While you hover, the animals and lines that are not near the one under the pointer turn grey.

Conditions

A column whose name starts with affected is a condition. With one such column, an animal whose value is TRUE (or 1) is filled pink, FALSE (or 0) leaves it white, and NA fills it grey, so that an animal whose status is not known does not look unaffected; the legend then has a grey row “Affected status unknown”. Hovering over an animal says Yes, No or Unknown. Here D and G are affected, and whether H is affected is not known.

fam1 <- fam
fam1$affected <- c(FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, NA)
layout1 <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam1)
drawPedigreeDiagram(layout1)

With two to four condition columns, each symbol is cut into one section per condition, filled in that condition’s colour where the animal is affected, and each condition’s row in the legend shows the sections with its own filled; a section whose status is not known is grey. The sections go counter-clockwise from the top, in the order of the columns. The column’s name gives the label: affected_diabetes becomes “Affected (diabetes)”. The drawing grows 45 pixels taller for each condition past the first, and for the “Affected status unknown” row, to make room in the legend. Here C has diabetes, B and E are obese, and A has arthritis; G has diabetes and is obese, and whether H is obese is not known, so H’s obesity section is grey.

fam3 <- fam
fam3$affected_diabetes  <- c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE,
                             FALSE)
fam3$affected_obesity   <- c(FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, NA)
fam3$affected_arthritis <- c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE,
                             FALSE)
layout3 <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam3)
layout3$conditions
#>               column                label   color
#> 1  affected_diabetes  Affected (diabetes) #CC79A7
#> 2   affected_obesity   Affected (obesity) #E69F00
#> 3 affected_arthritis Affected (arthritis) #56B4E9
drawPedigreeDiagram(layout3)

A fifth condition column and any after it are not drawn: the layout names them in conditionsNotDrawn.

fam5 <- fam3
fam5$affected_cataract     <- FALSE
fam5$affected_hypertension <- FALSE
layout5 <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam5)
layout5$conditions$label
#> [1] "Affected (diabetes)"  "Affected (obesity)"   "Affected (arthritis)"
#> [4] "Affected (cataract)"
layout5$conditionsNotDrawn
#> [1] "affected_hypertension"

Twins

Twins are listed in a table of their own, one pair per row: id1, id2 and code, which is "MZ twin", "DZ twin" or "UZ twin" (identical, fraternal or unknown). checkTwinRelations() stops if a pair is not possible: MZ and DZ twins must have the same sire and dam, and MZ twins the same sex. The layout takes the table as twinRelations and draws a green line between the two animals of each pair: solid and labelled “MZ”, dashed and labelled “DZ”, or with long dashes and labelled “?”.

litter <- data.frame(
  id   = c("S1", "D1", "A1", "A2", "B1", "B2", "C1", "C2"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1", "S1"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1", "D1"),
  sex  = c("M", "F", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M", "M")
)
litter$gen <- findGeneration(litter$id, litter$sire, litter$dam)
twins <- data.frame(
  id1  = c("A1", "B1", "C1"),
  id2  = c("A2", "B2", "C2"),
  code = c("MZ twin", "DZ twin", "UZ twin")
)
twins <- checkTwinRelations(litter, twins)
twinLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(litter, twinRelations = twins)
drawPedigreeDiagram(twinLayout)

Animals drawn twice

An animal is drawn in its own row under its sire and dam. When it mates with an animal that also has parents in the pedigree, one of the two is drawn a second time, beside the other, and a dashed line joins its two places. Here C, an offspring of A and B, and R, an offspring of P and Q, are the parents of S and T.

two <- data.frame(
  id   = c("A", "B", "C", "P", "Q", "R", "S", "T"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", NA, NA, "P", "C", "C"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "B", NA, NA, "Q", "R", "R"),
  sex  = c("M", "F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "F", "M")
)
two$gen <- findGeneration(two$id, two$sire, two$dam)
twoLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(two)
twoLayout$duplicateToReal
#> __dup_R_1 
#>       "R"
drawPedigreeDiagram(twoLayout)

R is drawn under her parents P and Q, and again beside her mate C, where S and T are drawn under their mating. The layout’s duplicateToReal names each repeat node and the animal it stands for, and hovering over a repeat says “(duplicate occurrence)”.

Matings of relatives

When a sire and dam are related, that is when their kinship coefficient is above 0, the two lines from them to their mating are drawn thick and orange; kinship2 draws a double line. Here C and D are full siblings, with a kinship coefficient of 0.25, so D is drawn again beside C.

sibs <- data.frame(
  id   = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "K"),
  sire = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", "C"),
  dam  = c(NA, NA, "B", "B", "D"),
  sex  = c("M", "F", "M", "F", "F")
)
sibs$gen <- findGeneration(sibs$id, sibs$sire, sibs$dam)
sibsLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(sibs)
drawPedigreeDiagram(sibsLayout)

Two edge styles

edgeStyle = "direct" draws a straight line from each parent to the mating dot and from the dot to each offspring, instead of lines at right angles. The animals and the dots stay where they were. Give drawPedigreeDiagram() the same edgeStyle: it sets how far the highlight reaches when you hover.

direct <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam, edgeStyle = "direct")
drawPedigreeDiagram(direct, edgeStyle = "direct")

Animals with no relative

An animal with no known parent, no offspring and no twin has nothing to join it to the others, so the layout leaves it out, says so in a message, and lists it in isolatedIds.

withZ <- rbind(fam, data.frame(id = "Z", sire = NA, dam = NA, sex = "M",
                               gen = 0L))
zLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(withZ)
#> makePedigreeMatingLayout(): 1 individual(s) with no recorded parents, mates, or offspring suppressed from the pedigree diagram: Z
zLayout$isolatedIds
#> [1] "Z"

Two animals that have mated but have no offspring together are not left out when the matings argument names them, one row per mating with its sire and dam: they are drawn side by side on one row, joined at a mating dot with no line down, as kinship2 and Pedixplorer draw a declared mating. The dot’s hover text reads “0 offspring”. Here Y is Z’s mate.

withYZ <- rbind(withZ, data.frame(id = "Y", sire = NA, dam = NA, sex = "F",
                                  gen = 0L))
yzLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(
  withYZ, matings = data.frame(sire = "Z", dam = "Y")
)
drawPedigreeDiagram(yzLayout)

Layout hints

The layout chooses the order of siblings and of families, and, for two animals with parents of their own, which one their offspring are drawn under. Layout hints change these choices. hints is a list with order, mate or both, in the form kinship2 and Pedixplorer give them.

order is a number for each animal, named by its id. Siblings, separate families and founder couples are drawn left to right in increasing order of their numbers; an animal without a number keeps its row’s place. Here E, D and C are drawn in that order, and C’s mate F and their offspring move with him.

orderLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(
  fam, hints = list(order = c(C = 3, D = 2, E = 1))
)
drawPedigreeDiagram(orderLayout)

mate is a data frame with one row per mating to place. left and right are its two animals, left drawn left of right, and anchor names the one under whose own place their offspring are drawn: "left", "right", or "either" for the layout’s own choice. Here the anchor is R, so C, not R, is drawn twice, and S and T are drawn under R’s place.

mateLayout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(
  two,
  hints = list(mate = data.frame(left = "C", right = "R", anchor = "right"))
)
drawPedigreeDiagram(mateLayout)

The layout returns the hints it used as hints, in the same form, so an edit can start from the layout’s own choices; passed back, they give the same layout. order numbers each animal that has a parent by its row (a founder gets a number only where an order named it, since naming one turns off the layout’s own order of founder lines). mate has the rows given, then a row for each other mating as drawn, except the matings of an animal with three or more of them, where a row can move its mates.

layout$hints
#> $order
#> C D E G H 
#> 3 4 5 7 8 
#> 
#> $mate
#>   left right anchor
#> 1    A     B   left
#> 2    C     F   left
identical(makePedigreeMatingLayout(fam, hints = layout$hints), layout)
#> [1] TRUE

kinship2 and Pedixplorer objects

asPedFrame() converts a kinship2 pedigree or a Pedixplorer Pedigree to the data frame, the twins table and the hints that the layout takes. kinship2 keeps hints in the object’s hints element: order, and spouse, a matrix with a row for each mating to place, holding the places (row numbers) of its left and right animal and the anchor, 1 for left, 2 for right and 0 for either. Here they are set by hand to show their form; kinship2::autohint() makes them for kinship2’s own layout, and gives these same hints for this pedigree. Add the generations before the layout. The chunks below run only when kinship2 or Pedixplorer is installed.

p <- kinship2::pedigree(
  id = two$id, dadid = two$sire, momid = two$dam,
  sex = ifelse(two$sex == "M", "male", "female")
)
p$hints <- list(order = 1:8, spouse = matrix(c(3, 6, 2), ncol = 3))
x <- asPedFrame(p)
x$hints
#> $order
#> A B C P Q R S T 
#> 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 
#> 
#> $mate
#>   left right anchor
#> 1    C     R  right
x$ped$gen <- findGeneration(x$ped$id, x$ped$sire, x$ped$dam)
k2Layout <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(x$ped, hints = x$hints)
identical(k2Layout$nodes, mateLayout$nodes)
#> [1] TRUE

The layout is the one drawn above for the mate hint. Pedixplorer keeps the same hints as horder, already named by id, and spouse, a data frame of idl, idr and anchor:

px <- Pedixplorer::Pedigree(
  data.frame(id = two$id, dadid = two$sire, momid = two$dam,
             sex = ifelse(two$sex == "M", "male", "female")),
  hints = list(horder = setNames(1:8, two$id),
               spouse = data.frame(idl = "C", idr = "R", anchor = 2))
)
y <- asPedFrame(px)
y$hints
#> $order
#> A B C P Q R S T 
#> 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 
#> 
#> $mate
#>   left right anchor
#> 1    C     R  right

Both packages’ automatic hints are made for their own layouts, and some of their mate rows are ones the layout refuses; asPedFrame() fixes those, and a message names each change.

Saving a drawing

A drawing is an htmlwidget, so htmlwidgets::saveWidget() saves it as a web page that any browser opens, with its sections and slashes. The “Export Diagram (PNG)” button at the bottom right of each drawing saves a picture of the drawing as you see it, as pedigree_diagram.png.

diagram <- drawPedigreeDiagram(layout)
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(diagram, "pedigree.html")

Clicks in a Shiny application

A click on a drawing does nothing unless onClick gives a JavaScript function to run. In a Shiny application it can send the id of the node clicked to the server. The drawing needs 500 pixels of height, 45 more for each condition past the first.

## In the user interface:
visNetwork::visNetworkOutput("pedigree", height = "500px")

## In the server function:
output$pedigree <- visNetwork::renderVisNetwork({
  drawPedigreeDiagram(layout, onClick = paste(
    "function(params) {",
    "Shiny.setInputValue('pedigreeClick', params.nodes);",
    "}"
  ))
})
shiny::observeEvent(input$pedigreeClick, {
  print(input$pedigreeClick)
})

params.nodes holds the id of the node clicked: an animal’s id, a repeat node’s, which duplicateToReal turns into its animal’s, or a mating dot’s, which starts with __union_.

A colony-size drawing

The example pedigree that comes with the package (vignette("pedkindraw")) has 375 rhesus macaques in nine generations, and three twin pairs.

pedFile <- system.file("extdata", "obfuscated_rhesus_mhc_ped.csv",
                       package = "pedkindraw")
twinFile <- system.file("extdata", "obfuscated_rhesus_mhc_twin_relations.csv",
                        package = "pedkindraw")
ped <- read.csv(pedFile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
colonyTwins <- read.csv(twinFile, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
ped$gen <- findGeneration(ped$id, ped$sire, ped$dam)
colony <- makePedigreeMatingLayout(ped, twinRelations = colonyTwins)
#> Warning: makePedigreeMatingLayout(): 72 same-row edge-node collision(s) could
#> not be fully resolved (residual after the repair-pass cap, or a curved
#> connector whose arc no roundness step fully clears) -- rendered output may
#> still show a straight or curved edge passing near an unrelated node.
drawPedigreeDiagram(colony)

The warning says that in 72 places a line may pass close to an animal it does not belong to: in the right-angle style the layout steps a line around an animal in its way, and these it could not fully clear. Nothing is missing from the drawing; all 375 animals are in it.

Fitted to the page, the drawing is too small to read its ids. Zoom in to read them, or pick an animal in the “Select by id” box: the animals and lines that are not near it turn grey, which shows where it is. The arcs are the dashed lines that join each of the 113 animals drawn more than once to its other places.

How large a drawing can be

Most of the time a drawing takes goes to the layout, in R. In measurements made in November 2026 on one Mac (Apple M2 Max), nprcgenekeepr’s drawing, from which pedkindraw’s is copied, drew 1,000 animals in about 16 seconds, and 2,000 animals not within two minutes. At 1,000 animals an animal could still be found by its id, and its lines followed to its parents, once zoomed in.

Where next

The help pages of makePedigreeMatingLayout() and drawPedigreeDiagram() give every argument, among them kinshipMatrix, which passes the layout kinship coefficients you have computed; ?asPedFrame gives each conversion, and vignette("pedkindraw") the rest of the package.
